alignments.note: גַּם → *also*; the ASV writes it postpositively, so the unit is discontinuous from the pronoun's rendering (rule 25).
The fronted independent pronoun is rendered by the whole expression *as for me*, which realizes that pronoun and nothing else; headed on the pronoun *me* that directly carries it (rule 24).
Negative לֹא → *not*; the ASV writes the modal as a separate word, so nothing is indivisible here (rule 35).
Verb with its auxiliary (rule 17), discontinuous around the negative (rule 25), headed on the lexical *spare*.
Waw plus the negative fused into the single English *neither* (rule 35), headed on the negative. The ASV writes no answering *nor*, so this is rule 35's fusion rather than rule 14's correlative pair.
Verb rendered by the light verb *have* plus its complement, with the subject pronoun and modal (rules 17, 44); headed on *pity*, since *have* alone has anything.
3mp suffix → *their* (rule 18); MACULA's glosses on s014/s015 are distributed in reverse order and are a display defect (rule 39).

No conjunction stands in this clause — it opens with the fronted object דַּרְכָּם — so no morpheme licenses the ASV's *but*, and it is its own added unit (rules 30, 51). It is not folded into the verb, for the reason rule 51 gives about a supplied *also*: the word is written beside that rendering rather than inside it.
Verb with its subject pronoun and modal (rule 17), headed on the lexical *bring*.

review_notes: The clause-initial *but* (t016) is added: the Hebrew clause has no waw or other conjunction, which rule 51's second half makes the deciding test.
s003 takes the whole *as for me*; the pronoun is fronted and no other morpheme answers to those words, while גַּם keeps its own postposed *also*.
